PagerDutyBot: URGENT: [PD-INC-8921] queue_backlog_high for service=realtime-inference - queue_length=14250, avg_queue_time=18.2s, error_rate=1.9% - auto-scaling attempted

IncidentBot: page fired to @Anna (oncall), @Ben (eng-sre) — escalation policy level 1 -> level 2. Pager: PagerDuty playbook started.

Anna (oncall): acked. I'm on it. First quick check: which pool is saturated? any customer-facing lanes impacted? :eyes:

Ben (eng-sre): seeing it across realtime GPU pool "realtime-gpupool-1". Autoscaler metrics show no new nodes requested for last 6m, observed kube events: many Pending pods due to insufficient GPU resources.

Ben (eng-sre): paste of kubectl/top and queue stats:
```
NAME                               CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)   GPU   REPLICAS
realtime-gpupool-1                 8500m        60Gi            8     12
Pending pods: 47
Queue length (per shard): [4800, 6200, 3250]
Autoscaler status:
scaleFactor: 0.75
lastEval: 2026-03-14T02:05:12Z
reason: maxNodeBudgetReached
```

Sarah (runtime): autoscaler hitting the max_node_budget threshold from last deploy (we tightened budgets). Policy prevented more nodes from being provisioned. Also we're seeing long GC pauses on a subset of model workers causing KV cache hotlocks.

Mike (prodops): customer impact: elevated latency for streaming responses (~+400ms tail) and ~1.9% 503s in the last 10m. Major customers on dedicated capacity unaffected, hosted API customers on realtime pool see errors. Triage priority: prevent further 503s.

Anna (oncall): OK, mitigation plan options: 1) temporarily raise max_node_budget, 2) force manual scale up (add nodes), 3) route low-priority traffic to fallback model variant/CPU pool, 4) shed non-critical features (batch rerank). Which is fastest?

Ben (eng-sre): fastest is manual scale via cloud provider (we have warm nodes ready but budget limit prevented use). I can run manual scaleup now. Command I will run:
```bash
redwoodctl infra aws scale --pool realtime-gpupool-1 --nodes +8 --reason "emergency autoscale bypass"
```

Sarah (runtime): also recommend flipping routing rule for non-prod customers and opt-in beta to fallback:
```yaml
routing:
  - match: traffic.priority == low
    action: route_to: realtime-gpupool-fallback
    weight: 1.0
```
This will drop lower-priority load off the saturated pool.

Mike (prodops): +1 on routing. I'll create a temporary SLA exception for legal for high-volume customers so we can divert traffic. Also we should enable pre-warmed nodes for realtime pool after we stabilize.

Ben (eng-sre): executed manual scale command — infra API accepted. New nodes requested: 8, expected join window 3-5m. Watching kube events.

IncidentBot: escalation to level 2 sent to @Mike (prodops) due to >1% error_rate sustained for 10m.

Anna (oncall): I'm going to throttle internal batch tasks: disabling noncritical batch rerank and background evals. On it.

Anna (oncall): ran: `redwoodctl jobs pause --tag=batch-rerank` -> job queue drained from 320 -> 20 in 90s.

Ben (eng-sre): new nodes started joining at 02:12Z, kube join log snippet:
```
I0314 02:12:34.123 Joined node ip-10-0-5-32 with 4 GPUs
I0314 02:13:05.210 Joined node ip-10-0-5-33 with 4 GPUs
```
Scheduler started binding pending pods, pending count down from 47 -> 12 in 2m.

Sarah (runtime): KV cache hotlock metric decreasing. Memory pressure easing on several pods. I recommend increasing worker concurrency gradually to avoid another spike.

Ben (eng-sre): queue length now: [3200, 1800, 900] — avg_queue_time -> 6.2s. Error rate down to 0.4%. Looks like manual scale + job pause worked.

PagerDutyBot: alert status: acknowledged -> in_progress. Incident window started at 02:03Z.

Mike (prodops): starting a temporary routing rule now to shift 30% low-priority traffic to CPU fallback. Will monitor for SLA/backfill impacts.

Anna (oncall): handoff note: I'm going offline for a planned break at 02:25Z. Ben — please take primary for next 30m, escalate to Sarah if we see GC spikes again. I'll leave runbook links: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/autoscaler-queue-backlog and incident channel.

Ben (eng-sre): taking over. Setting Slack status. Will watch metrics and follow up on root cause (budget limit + GC behavior).

Sarah (runtime): follow-up: opened PR to relax max_node_budget temporarily and added a telemetry alert to detect autoscaler saturation (new metric: autoscaler_budget_blocked_count). PR link: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/3245

Anna (oncall): thanks team. After 30m we should run a post-incident check: verify scaling policy, increase default max_node_budget for realtime pools, and review GC tuning for model workers. I'll file an incident report draft. :memo:

Mike (prodops): logged a customer-impact ticket and notified CS for outreach.

Ben (eng-sre): last status at 02:28Z: queue lengths stabilizing, error_rate 0.2%, autoscaler now evaluating new budget. I'll collect kube events and attach to postmortem.

IncidentBot: incident marked: mitigated (manual scale + routing). Escalation cleared.

Anna (oncall): closing active page. Follow-up actions: 1) revert emergency scaling after confirmation (or keep if needed), 2) merge PR to avoid future budget blocks, 3) add playbook step to flip routing for low-prio traffic. I'll update tickets. :white_check_mark:
